sources.entry: pyodide - Python distribution for the browser and Node.js based on WebAssembly.

summary.one_liner: Pyodide is a port of CPython to WebAssembly that lets Python run and install packages in the browser and Node.js.
summary.what_it_does: Pyodide is a Python distribution built by porting CPython to WebAssembly/Emscripten. It lets users install and run Python packages in the browser with micropip, and the README says any pure Python package with a wheel on PyPI is supported. Many packages with C, C++, and Rust extensions have been ported, including regex, PyYAML, cryptography, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn. It provides a JavaScript-to-Python foreign function interface with error handling and async/await support. When running in a browser, Python has access to the Web APIs. The project also includes a toolchain for cross-compiling and installing packages for Pyodide.
use_cases: run Python code in a web page without a server
install and use NumPy, pandas, or Matplotlib in the browser
call JavaScript functions from Python and vice versa
port or test a Python package for WebAssembly
embed a Python REPL in a website
how_to_run: Use a hosted distribution: see the Getting Started documentation
Or download a release from the releases page and serve it with a web server
Use with a bundler: see the Working with Bundlers documentation
Build from source: see the building Pyodide from source documentation
notable: Runs CPython in the browser and Node.js via WebAssembly
Supports many C, C++, and Rust extension packages such as NumPy, pandas, and SciPy
Two-way JavaScript and Python foreign function interface with async/await
Python code can access Web APIs when running in a browser
Originated in 2018 at Mozilla as part of the Iodide project
caveats: The README says Iodide, the project it originated from, is no longer maintained
Only packages ported to Pyodide can use C, C++, or Rust extensions; others depend on pure Python wheels
The README does not state platform or performance limits
